title: STORK: Faster Diffusion and Flow Matching Sampling by Resolving both Stiffness and Structure-Dependence
claim: At extremely low step budgets, baseline samplers yield artifacts, wrong text and missing prompt elements, while ours renders faithful, detailed, prompt-matching images.
layout: 4 rows by 4 columns of image grids, baselines left and ours rightmost, prompt and commentary caption under each row
description: A tall figure of four rows of four square generated images each. Each row shares one text prompt, printed in monospace beneath the row, followed by a short serif commentary line explaining why the rightmost image is better. The first three images in each row come from baseline samplers and the fourth from STORK. Row one shows a cyberpunk stork holding a plaque. Baselines misspell the word as 'stonk', 'strokr' or 'stoki', while STORK writes 'Stork' with finer feather detail. Row two shows a cowboy singer on horseback. Baselines are dark and silhouetted, while STORK is bright and vivid. Row three shows a Joker logo with the letter Q. Only STORK includes both. Row four shows a nostalgia scene. Baselines are less coherent, while STORK has a rich arrangement of many retro objects. The eye goes first to the vivid images in the right column.
caption: Comparison between the Flow-Euler, Flow-DPM-Solver++ [ref], Flow-UniPC [ref], and STORK. All images are generated using the SANA 1.6B model [ref] at $1024\times 1024$ resolution with only 8 NFEs. Prompts are displayed beneath each image pair, accompanied by our commentary explaining why STORK's generations are superior. STORK achieves much better visual fidelity at the extremely low NFE case, showing its effectiveness as a fast sampling method. Zoom in for better visual details.
abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) and flow-matching models have demonstrated remarkable performance in image and video generation. However, such models require a significant number of function evaluations (NFEs) during sampling, leading to costly inference. Consequently, quality-preserving fast sampling methods that require fewer NFEs have been an active area of research. However, prior training-free sampling methods fail to simultaneously address two key challenges: the stiffness of the ODE (i.e., the non-straightness of the velocity field) and dependence on the semi-linear structure of the DM ODE (which limits their direct applicability to flow-matching models). In this work, we introduce the Stabilized Taylor Orthogonal Runge--Kutta (STORK) method, addressing both design concerns. We demonstrate that STORK consistently improves the quality of diffusion and flow-matching sampling for image and video generation. Code is available at https://github.com/ZT220501/STORK.
